events.title: Wiley Post Completes First Solo Round-the-World Flight
events.description: American aviator Wiley Post landed at Floyd Bennett Field in New York in his Lockheed Vega, the Winnie Mae, after circling the globe alone in about 7 days and 19 hours.
events.significance: The feat demonstrated the growing capabilities of long-distance aviation and navigation, and it paved the way for later high-altitude and long-range flight research.

events.title: John Dillinger Shot Dead by FBI Agents
events.description: Notorious bank robber John Dillinger, labeled Public Enemy No. 1, was gunned down by federal agents outside the Biograph Theater in Chicago after being betrayed by an associate.
events.significance: His death was a landmark moment in the FBI's campaign against Depression-era outlaws and helped boost the public profile and powers of the Bureau under J. Edgar Hoover.

events.title: Bretton Woods Conference Concludes
events.description: Delegates from 44 Allied nations finished the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference in New Hampshire, agreeing to establish the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank).
events.significance: The agreements created the framework for the postwar international monetary system, including fixed exchange rates tied to the US dollar, and shaped global economic governance for decades.

events.title: Jeffrey Dahmer Arrested in Milwaukee
events.description: Police arrested Jeffrey Dahmer after a would-be victim escaped and led officers to his apartment, where evidence of a series of murders was discovered.
events.significance: The arrest ended a killing spree that claimed 17 lives and prompted widespread scrutiny of police response and treatment of marginalized communities.

events.title: Norway Attacks in Oslo and Utøya
events.description: A right-wing extremist detonated a bomb in Oslo's government quarter, killing eight people, then carried out a mass shooting at a Workers' Youth League summer camp on Utøya island, killing 69 more.
events.significance: It was the deadliest attack in Norway since World War II, leading to national mourning, a reassessment of security and emergency response, and a widely noted public commitment to democratic values.
